reasoning: The accepted work was exactly to make the grader treat an extra act as a failure rather than a note. The four runs that now read red are that instruction working: every one of them carries the extra act the person ordered counted as a failure, so the score movement from 30 to 26 is the observable outcome of the admitted done, not a side effect reaching past it. The pipeline's rule is explicit that a redefinition he ordered himself is not the reserved third case — he settled that fork when he ordered it, and carrying it out is executing his decision, not making one. Nothing here is a taste call, no artifact-unsettled trade-off stands open, and the change is reversible in git. Nothing is broken, no check inside the admitted scope is red, and the unit tests pass, so the accepted scope holds no todo, missing artifact or red check. Under the closing kernel the row is closed against the definition of done it was admitted on, never against what shipped: a verifier who did not produce the work is handed the observable outcome and the paths touched, writes the receipt with the commands and their exit codes, and close reads that receipt. A shown result closes the work; his own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery, and the re-graded score belongs in the report — what it said before, what it says now — so he can disagree while undoing is still cheap. If he then disagrees with the new score line, that disagreement is a new fact and its own task, not a reopening of this one.
